# Research Overview: Novel Faith/Religious Software Newly Buildable Because of 2024-2026 AI

## Summary

This run was a deep, single-category drive into faith/religious software — Phase 2 of a broader consumer-software
study whose central finding (capability is commoditized; the durable asset is a *structural wedge an incumbent
won't or can't copy*) we set out to test inside religion specifically. Across 8 rounds we stratified generation
across **nine traditions** (Christianity — Protestant/Catholic/Orthodox; Islam; Judaism; Sikh; Hindu; Buddhist;
interfaith/SBNR) and **~12 functional sub-niches** (scripture scholarship, prayer/devotion, worship/liturgy,
religious education, clergy ops, congregation/giving, apologetics, observance logistics, pilgrimage, sacred-text
scholarship, religious media). 26 hypotheses were generated; **5 were rejected at Perplexity-grounded peer review**
for already shipping, for a categorical legal/data barrier, or for a factually-false premise; the survivors were
ranked by a ~90-match Elo tournament.

**The headline finding: in faith-tech the losing move is "a chatbot on a holy book," and the winning move is a
load-bearing 2024-26 AI capability fused to a *private, compounding, or structurally-walled-off asset* — sold to a
budget-holding religious professional in a recurring or mandatory workflow.** Every idea whose only wedge was
retrieval-augmented Q&A, white-label doctrine chat, or sermon-clip generation either was rejected outright or sank
